headline: Approved June 8 minutes unanimously and scheduled a remote special meeting to approve a Hispanic Heritage Month proclamation.
summary: The committee checked in after the shooting of Biddeford resident Johan Sebastian Duran Guerrero. It discussed the June events, the public restroom survey, the City Charter, and a Public Art Commission request for feedback.
decisions: Approved the June 8, 2026 meeting minutes by unanimous vote.
Scheduled a remote meeting at 11:45 AM on September 1 to approve the proclamation.

decision_titles: Remote meeting on September 1 to approve proclamation
plain_text:
August 10, 2026 Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Committee Meeting Minutes 
Present: Flo, Anne, David, Jamie, Aiden, 1 Member of Public 
Excused: Lauren, Syed, Ariane, Breese 
 
1. Call to Order 
Meeting called to order at 5:31 PM.  
 
2. Public Comment 
One member of the public introduced herself to the Committee. 
The Chair introduced the peacekeepers that were asked to attend the meeting. 
 
3. Approval of Minutes 
3.a June 8, 2026 Meeting Minutes 
 Motion by Aiden, seconded by Jamie, to approve the June 8, 2026 meeting minutes. 
 Vote: Unanimous 
 
4. Current Events 
4.a Member Check-In 
The Committee checked in with one another after the events of the past month, 
specifically the shooting of Biddeford resident, Johan Sebastian Duran Guerrero. 
Members shared their feelings and reactions to the incident and the City and 
community responses that followed. 
Anne noted that there is a higher level of scrutiny on our community and work. She 
would like to reach out to some mental health support services for those who are 
most impacted by the level of scrutiny. 
Aiden has a resource list of people and organizations that are offering free or low-
cost therapy services for those who have been affected by ICE’s presence in the 
area. He will share this list with the Committee.
David noted that Sweetser’s mental health team, in conjunction with the General 
Assistance office, offered crisis support immediately following the incident.  
Flo feels it is hard to talk about long-term projects right now when there is an 
immediate event to react to. Aiden suggested we could put some of those projects 
off given the context of current events. 
Flo mentioned that there is a concurrent meeting this evening about the City 
Charter and wondered if the Committee could look at it through a DEI lens. David 
said that the Committee’s perspective would be very valuable to the conversation. 
He mentioned Council compensation as a topic for the committee to potentially 
weigh in on. 
Flo suggested that we have a member check-in at each meeting.  
 
5. Discussion Items 
5.a Review of Proclamations and Observances - September and October 
Anne offered to draft the Hispanic Heritage Month proclamation and will 
incorporate recent events into the language that has been used for previous 
proclamations. 
The Committee discussed the timeline for approval of the proclamation in 
comparison to the timing of the next regularly-scheduled meeting. David suggested 
calling a special meeting to approve the proclamation. The Committee opted to 
have a remote meeting at 11:45 AM on September 1 to approve the proclamation.  
 
5.b Reflection on June Events 
Flo thought it was gratifying that this was the first time that the Committee took 
ownership the Pride flag raising event as the official organizers. She was proud of 
Jamie for jumping in at the last minute to emcee the event. 
Anne thought the Tiger Allies were a highlight of the event. David shared a positive 
interaction with a kid on a bus driving by. Flo was glad that the event happened on 
June 1. 
David noted that some individuals intentionally rev their engines during the event 
and thought we could consider closing a street next year. Anne suggested we notify
City staff about the event next year to give them an opportunity to come out and 
participate for a few minutes if they’d like. 
The Juneteenth event netted a profit of $1,030 after donations. Heart of Biddeford 
would usually take 3% of the total income from the event to cover their overhead, 
which would be $139. The Committee was supportive of making this payment. This 
leaves $891 to use for next year’s event. 
There were 171 registrations with 60 donations coming through, and estimated 
headcounts indicate that there were more attendees that were present but did not 
register. There were 21 spoof registrations for the event. Heart of Biddeford received 
pushback for the verbiage on their EventBrite registration page related to the 
encouraged donations, and this language will be revisited for clarity.  
Flo would like us to keep the award presentation for next year. Members discussed 
a possible candidate for the award. 
 
5.c Public Restroom Survey 
Anne shared information about a rule out of Louisiana requiring people to use the 
same restroom of the gender that they were assigned at birth. She believes that 
these kinds of rules and laws are likely to catch on in other places. She noted that 
this was relevant to the public restroom conversation as well as the Charter 
conversation. 
Flo asked the Committee to read the charter between now and the next meeting if 
they have time. 
David noted that the Charter Revision Commission makes a recommendation on 
changes to the charter, and voters ultimately adopt the changes they propose. They 
can either put all of them together in one question to voters or can present different 
changes individually.  
The attending member of the public noted that Better Biddeford is looking to 
schedule a salon to discuss the charter. She invited members of the Committee to 
attend. 
 
5.d Request for Feedback on Public Art Master Plan
The Committee received an email from the Public Art Commission seeking 
feedback.  
Jamie attended the Public Art Commission’s June meeting. She reported that the 
Commission talked about their Master Plan and noted that they would like to 
collaborate more often with the DEI Committee, though they have nothing specific 
in the queue that they would like to work on with us right now. They mentioned that 
if our members know artists of diverse backgrounds that are interested in public art 
pieces, they would like us to refer them to their Commission. Flo noted that a 
partnership with the Public Art Commission would be fitting as we plan for the June 
events next year and suggested we invite them to a future meeting. 
 
6. Other Business 
No other business was discussed. 
 
7. Second Public Comment 
The attending member of the public noted that the old courthouse located on Adams 
Street has a lobby area that may be suitable for use as a public restroom facility. She 
encouraged the Committee to reach out to the City and Biddeford Housing Authority to 
start a discussion about this. She anticipates that a conversation about how to keep them 
clean and maintained will be the biggest concern and suggested that a plan is made for 
that before a pitch is made. 
 
8. Adjourn 
Meeting adjourned at 7:01.
